title: feat(N1): NIP-05 verification via Namecoin (.bit identifiers) — draft for #363
body:
Draft PR for #363.

## What this does

Adds opt-in NIP-05 verification of `.bit` / `d/<name>` / `id/<name>` identifiers against the Namecoin blockchain, via an ElectrumX-NMC WebSocket transport (no raw TCP, no native deps, works on Flutter Android out of the box).

Today `ProfileIdentityRow` renders `profile.nip05` next to an unconditional check icon — there's no underlying verification step at all (no DNS resolution, no `.well-known/nostr.json` fetch, no signature/pubkey match). This PR adds verification for the `.bit` subset and surfaces the outcome in explicit per-state UI (verified / mismatch / unverified / unreachable / resolving / not-applicable).

DNS-based NIP-05 verification is **out of scope** — that is a separate gap and a separate conversation.

## Why draft

Per the README ("please reach out to us first") and the spec-first workflow in `spec/guidelines/QUALITY_BAR.md` ("behavior changes require a feature spec first"), this is staged as a draft for design review. Issue #363 is the proposal; this PR is the staging diff so you can see exactly what changes if it lands.

Happy to:
- Convert the work packet to a feature spec under `spec/features/` if preferred
- Move the badge placement / styling
- Pin the default ElectrumX server set to something Zapstore-controlled
- Or close this if it's not aligned

## Architecture fit

Per `spec/guidelines/ARCHITECTURE.md`:
- All new code lives under `lib/services/namecoin/` and `lib/widgets/common/` — UI-facing orchestration, not domain logic
- No `models` or `purplebase` change
- No relay-pool or storage touch
- `ProfileIdentityRow` is unchanged for non-`.bit` identifiers (no regression risk)

Per `spec/guidelines/INVARIANTS.md`:
- UI thread never blocks (async + `FutureProvider.autoDispose`)
- Every error maps to a sealed-class state — no silent failures
- Mismatched on-chain pubkeys are an *explicit* state, not a fall-through to "verified"
- Parser tolerates malformed/unknown/future fields (covered by tests)

## What's in the diff

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `lib/services/namecoin/electrumx_client.dart` | WebSocket transport (ported from dart-nostr#44, CC0) |
| `lib/services/namecoin/electrumx_server.dart` | Default server list |
| `lib/services/namecoin/script.dart` | Namecoin script parser |
| `lib/services/namecoin/value.dart` | NIP-N0 `nostr` field extractor |
| `lib/services/namecoin/identifier.dart` | `.bit` / `d/` / `id/` parser |
| `lib/services/namecoin/record_parser.dart` | Host-flat splitter, relay/tor walkers (TLSA deferred to N3) |
| `lib/services/namecoin/namecoin_nip05_service.dart` | Riverpod-friendly service with sealed-class state model |
| `lib/widgets/common/namecoin_nip05_badge.dart` | Replacement NIP-05 row with verification badge |
| `lib/widgets/common/profile_identity_row.dart` | One-line swap to use the new badge |
| `pubspec.yaml` | Promotes `crypto` and `convert` to direct deps (both were transitive) |
| `spec/work/WORK-N1-namecoin-nip05.md` | Work packet (per AGENTS.md) |
| `test/services/namecoin/record_parser_test.dart` | 18 parser tests |
| `test/services/namecoin/namecoin_nip05_service_test.dart` | 12 service tests across every sealed state |

## Verification

```
flutter pub get      → clean
flutter analyze      → No issues found! (full project)
flutter test         → 47/47 passing (30 new + 17 pre-existing)
```

Tested on Flutter 3.41.4 / Dart 3.11.1 (not 3.38.6 from `.fvmrc` — host doesn't have FVM, but the SDK constraints in pubspec.yaml are satisfied; flagging for awareness).

## Reference implementation

The transport, parser, and identifier code are ported verbatim (CC0) from [ethicnology/dart-nostr#44](https://github.com/ethicnology/dart-nostr/pull/44) (merged) — same code that backs the Amethyst Android / KMP iOS / Desktop ports and the strfry sidecar. 526/526 tests pass in the upstream against live blockchain.

## Sibling proposals (open separately)

- #365 — N2: relay discovery via Namecoin (`wss://relay.example.bit`). Reuses this module's resolver.
- #364 — N3: TLSA pinning for `.bit` relay WebSockets. Reuses the parser, adds an enforcement layer.
- #362 — N4: Service attestations (kind 38383/38384). Independent surface; experimental.

This PR is fully independent of those three — review and merge order is up to you.

title: feat(N4): service attestation (kind 38383) ingest — experimental, draft for #362
body:
Draft PR for #362.

## What this does

Adds a **read-only ingest** path for NIP-N4 `kind:38383` service attestations:

* `ServiceAttestation` plain-Dart model
* Tolerant parser from `(attesterPubkey, createdAtSec, tags, content)` → model
* `dedupeAttestations()` — newest wins per `(attesterPubkey, dTag)`
* `AttestationSummary` — attester count, attestation count, average rating, Namecoin-anchored count
* `AttestationQueryService` — pulls `kind:38383` events from local storage and produces a summary
* `attestationSummaryProvider` Riverpod family for future UI consumption

## What this does *not* do — explicitly

Per the proposal in #362:

* **No UI surface.** No badge on the dev profile, no row on the app detail screen.
* **No influence on whitelisting / blocking / install.** Trust model is untouched.
* **No Namecoin anchor verification.** The `nmc` tag is parsed and counted but no chain query happens.

The proposal explicitly framed N4 as the one of the four most worth saying "not yet" to. This PR honours that — it lands the *reader* so the kind is ingestable when it stabilises, and otherwise has zero behavioural effect.

## Why ship anything at all?

Two reasons:

1. **Reference reader.** Having a working ingest path in a real Nostr app raises the bar for the kind to stabilise. The structural choices in the parser surface real questions about the NIP (e.g. should `rating` always be 0..1 normalised? what about `rating > max`?). Those questions can now be answered against running code, not slideware.
2. **Cheap to revert.** It is ~340 LOC of plain-Dart in a self-contained directory with no app-wide touch points. If N4 dies upstream, the directory deletes cleanly.

## Why draft

Same reason as #366 / #367 / #368 — per the README + spec-first workflow, this is for review not for merge. *Explicit invitation*: a "not now" close is a fine outcome. The proposal already disclosed N4 as least mature of the four.

## Architecture fit

- All new code under `lib/services/attestations/` — no app-wide touch.
- No `models` change. `ServiceAttestation` is plain Dart so this can ship without coordinated package releases.
- No `purplebase` change. Query uses the same `Request<Model<dynamic>>(...)` pattern that `deletion_processor.dart` already uses for ad-hoc kind queries.
- `LocalSource` only — service does not generate background network traffic when the feature is unused.

## What's in the diff

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `lib/services/attestations/attestation_models.dart` | `ServiceAttestation`, `AttestationSummary`, `NamecoinAttestationAnchor` |
| `lib/services/attestations/attestation_parser.dart` | Tolerant parser + `dedupeAttestations()` |
| `lib/services/attestations/attestation_query_service.dart` | Storage query + Riverpod provider |
| `spec/work/WORK-N4-service-attestations.md` | Work packet with experimental disclaimer |
| `test/services/attestations/attestation_parser_test.dart` | 18 tests covering parser, dedupe, summary |

title: feat(N3): Stage 1 TLSA pin parsing for .bit relays — draft for #364
body:
Draft PR for #364.

## What this does — Stage 1 only

Adds RFC 6698 TLSA pin **parsing** for `.bit` relay hostnames. `NamecoinTlsaService` fetches the on-chain record, parses any `tls` entries, and returns them in a sealed-class state model:

* `NotApplicable` — host is not `.bit`
* `PinsAvailable` — pins were parsed; ready to be enforced (separately)
* `NoPins` — record exists but has no TLSA entries
* `Unknown` — name not registered / expired / record unparseable
* `Unreachable` — every configured ElectrumX server failed

**No connection-time enforcement is added by this PR.** That is Stage 2 (see below).

## Why Stage 1 is shipped alone

Flutter's high-level `WebSocket` API does not expose the peer certificate. Enforcing pins needs either an Android platform channel into OkHttp's `CertificatePinner` or a custom `IOClient`/`SecurityContext` pipeline. Either path is invasive enough to warrant its own design conversation.

Per `spec/guidelines/QUALITY_BAR.md`: "Happy-path-only implementations are insufficient" — but it would be much worse to ship fake enforcement. This PR's API is honest: it tells you a pin exists and what it pins, but doesn't pretend to enforce it.

Stage 2 can ship as a follow-up; the Stage 1 API is stable across that transition.

## Why draft

Same reason as #366 / #367 — per the README + spec-first workflow, this is for review not for merge. Particular invitation for review here: **is Stage 1 alone interesting to land?** If the answer is "no, we'd rather hold this until Stage 2 is ready," that is a fine outcome and I'll close.

| `lib/services/namecoin/tlsa.dart` | RFC 6698 parser (ported CC0 from [dart-nostr#44](https://github.com/ethicnology/dart-nostr/pull/44)) |

title: feat(N2): Namecoin .bit relay hostname resolution — draft for #365
body:
Draft PR for #365.

## What this does

Adds support for `wss://relay.example.bit` style relay URLs in `RelayManagementCard`. When the user adds a `.bit` URL, a background ElectrumX lookup fires against the Namecoin chain and shows the resolved clearnet endpoint in a snackbar — so the user can see exactly what their chain-anchored hostname points at.

## Honest scope disclosure

This PR delivers two of the three pieces of the full N2 feature:

1. ✅ The **resolver** — `NamecoinRelayService` with a sealed-class state model.
2. ✅ The **user-visible preview** — snackbar at relay-add time.
3. ❌ **Actually connecting via the resolved endpoint** — owned by `purplebase` per `spec/guidelines/ARCHITECTURE.md` ("Relay pools and subscriptions are owned by purplebase"), out of scope for a zapstore-side PR.

Piece (3) is a follow-up that needs coordination across the zapstore→purplebase boundary. The two pieces shipped here are the directly-zapstore-owned parts: they're reusable by the same surface in (3) once that conversation happens.

## Why draft

Same reason as #366 — per the README and `QUALITY_BAR.md` spec-first workflow, staging the diff for review rather than asking for a merge.

## Architecture fit

- All new code under `lib/services/namecoin/` and the single touched call site (`addRelay`)
- No `purplebase` change
- No relay-pool touch
- Resolution is `unawaited()` so the existing add-relay UX is not blocked

## What's in the diff

| `lib/services/namecoin/*.dart` | Vendored resolver module (ported CC0 from [dart-nostr#44](https://github.com/ethicnology/dart-nostr/pull/44)). Identical to the module landed in #366 — TLSA parsing deferred to #364 |
| `lib/services/namecoin/namecoin_relay_service.dart` | Service with sealed-class state model |

## Verification

```

flutter analyze      → No issues found! (full project)
flutter test         → 44/44 passing
```

Tested on Flutter 3.41.4 / Dart 3.11.1 (not 3.38.6 from `.fvmrc` — host doesn't have FVM, but the SDK constraints in pubspec.yaml are satisfied; flagging for awareness).

## Sibling proposals

- #366 — N1 PR: NIP-05 verification via Namecoin. Shares the resolver module.
- #364 — N3: TLSA pinning. Would add cert-pin enforcement to the resolved connection.
- #362 — N4: Service attestations. Independent surface.

This PR is fully independent of those three. If #366 merges first the resolver files are already in tree; this PR's diff would shrink accordingly.

## What landing this enables next

Once piece (3) lands across the zapstore→purplebase boundary, the user's `wss://relay.example.bit` actually dials the resolved endpoint, so a developer can publish their `kind:32267` app events to a Namecoin-addressed relay and zapstore users can subscribe to it by typing the `.bit` hostname.

title: Add NIP-55 support
body:
This PR implements proper NIP-55 Android signer support using a new Dart package, nip55_signer. The nip55_signer package can detect all NIP-55 signer apps installed on the device, not just Amber. When signing in, it automatically uses the signer if only one is installed, or prompts the user to choose if multiple are available. The user's signer preference is remembered across app restarts, so they won't need to select again. Session data is stored securely using the device's native secure storage rather than as Nostr events.

title: Add opt-in crash reporting with NIP-17 encrypted delivery
body:
## Summary

Implements a privacy-focused crash reporting system using NIP-17 gift-wrapped encrypted messages.

- Crashes are cached locally and only sent after user consent
- Reports are encrypted using NIP-44 and wrapped with NIP-59 gift wrap protocol
- Ephemeral keys hide sender identity on relays
- NIP-40 expiration tags ensure auto-deletion after 30 days

## Changes

1. **Crash caching service** - Local file-based crash storage with rotation (max 3 reports)
2. **NIP-17 gift wrap service** - Privacy-preserving encrypted message delivery
3. **Consent UI** - Dialog prompts user on startup if crashes are cached
4. **Debug test button** - Test crash button in Profile (debug builds only)

## Architecture

```
Crash → Cache locally → App restart → Consent dialog → User approves → NIP-17 encrypted DM
```

title: Add CDN download option and hash mismatch fallback
body:
## Problem

Downloads go directly to the original URL (e.g. GitHub), exposing the user's IP to the host. Also, when a download fails hash verification, the user only sees an error with no automatic retry from another source.

## Solution

This PR implements both items from #60:

1. **Hash mismatch fallback**: When a download from the original URL fails hash verification, retry from cdn.zapstore.dev before showing an error. This handles transient corruption or CDN cache issues.

2. **Always download from CDN option**: A global setting lets users always download from cdn.zapstore.dev instead of the original URL, hiding their IP from GitHub and other hosts. The option appears in:
   - The trust dialog (switch "Download from CDN (hides IP)")
   - Settings ("Always download from CDN" toggle)

## Note

The UI/UX for these features should be reviewed by the UX/UI team before merge.

title: Backup and restore installed apps (Issue #20)
body:
**Closes #20**

### Problem

Users who reinstall Zapstore or switch devices lose the list of apps they had installed. There was no way to keep or restore that list.

We added backup and restore for installed apps using the same pattern as bookmarks: an encrypted AppStack (kind 30267) stored on Nostr social relays with NIP-44 encryption. Only apps that are both installed and in the Zapstore catalog are included.

**Backup:** Collects all cataloged installed apps, builds addressable IDs (`kind:pubkey:identifier`), encrypts them, and publishes to social relays.

**Restore:** Fetches the backup from relays, decrypts it, resolves IDs to App models, and shows a full-screen list split into "To install" and "Already installed", with an "Install All" option when there are multiple apps to install.

### Current UX

For now, backup and restore are manual actions via two tiles in Profile → Data Management: "Backup installed apps" and "Restore installed apps". Both require sign-in.

### Open decisions

1. **Automatic triggers:** It still needs to be decided if and when backup/restore should run automatically, for example:
   - On app startup (e.g. after sign-in)
   - On sign-in
   - When installing or uninstalling apps
   - On a schedule (e.g. periodic backup)

2. **UX/UI review:** The restore screen and Data Management section should be reviewed by the UX/UI team to confirm the flow and layout, and to suggest changes if needed.

title: fix: #319 install queue gets stuck with multiple concurrent downloads
body:
## Problem

When installing multiple apps at once (e.g. tapping several updates quickly), the install queue would get stuck — downloads completed but installs never started. After investigating, I found several bugs working together:

1. **Install slot never freed on orphan/sync paths** — if the native event arrived after sync already cleared the operation, `clearInstallSlot` was never called, permanently blocking the queue.

2. **InstallCancelled gets overwritten** — when the user dismissed the install dialog, the operation went to `InstallCancelled`, but native retries (verifying/started/pendingUserAction) would overwrite it back to an active state. The spec says InstallCancelled is terminal and only "Install (retry)" should exit it.

3. **Watchdog timer defeated by timestamp reset** — every `pendingUserAction` or `systemProcessing` event was creating a new operation object with a fresh `startedAt`, so the 2-minute watchdog timeout never fired. The operation would bounce between states forever.

4. **ReadyToInstall had no watchdog** — if the native side silently failed to respond after `triggerInstall`, the operation stayed in ReadyToInstall forever with no timeout.

5. **Android install dialog invisible** — `launchConfirmDialog` was using Application context with `FLAG_ACTIVITY_NEW_TASK`, which puts the dialog in a separate Android task. When the user is actively using the app, Android sometimes places it behind the current task, so the dialog never shows up.

6. **Batch progress banner wrong** — `InstallCancelled` operations were inflating the total count, showing e.g. "3 of 9" when only 6 apps were actually in the queue. Also the banner said "updated" even for new installs.

## Solution

All fixes follow the FEAT-001 spec (Package Manager), specially the "No Hanging States" invariant and the InstallCancelled behavior.

- Guard `_handleInstallEvent` to reject native events when operation is `InstallCancelled`
- Preserve `startedAt` timestamp when transitioning Installing → SystemProcessing and skip redundant state transitions
- Call `clearInstallSlot` in orphan handler and sync completion path
- Add `triggeredAt` to `ReadyToInstall` so the watchdog can monitor it
- Implement `ActivityAware` in the Kotlin plugin to get the Activity context, and launch the install dialog in the same task stack (no `FLAG_ACTIVITY_NEW_TASK`)
- Kotlin watchdog now re-launches the pending dialog when the app is in foreground
- Exclude `InstallCancelled` from batch totals, auto-clear terminal operations after 3s
- Dynamic label: "updated" for update batches, "installed" for new installs

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Fixed installation confirmation dialog not appearing when app returns to foreground
  * Completed operation banners now automatically dismiss after 3 seconds
  * Improved app state management to correctly distinguish between updates and new installations
  * Enhanced handling of installation states to prevent dialogs from disappearing unexpectedly

title: Fix Install/Delete buttons after install
body:
### Problem
After an app is installed, the main button switches to **Open** (correct), but the **Delete** button does not show right away. It only appears after leaving the screen and coming back.

In the flow **Install → Delete → Install again**, the UI could stay on **Open** or the second **Install** would not start.

This happens because `PackageManager` keeps a `Completed` operation for some time (needed for batch progress UX). The detail screen treated `Completed` like an active operation, so actions and re-install could be blocked.

### Fix
- Treat `Completed` as “not busy” on the app detail action row, so **Delete** shows immediately after install.
- Ignore stale `Completed` when the app is no longer installed, so the main CTA returns to **Install**.
- In `PackageManager.startDownload()`, clear stale terminal states (`Completed` / `OperationFailed`) so re-install works, while still blocking real in-flight operations.

### Result
- Delete shows immediately after install.
- After uninstall, the CTA goes back to Install.
- Install → Delete → Install again works without leaving the screen.

title: Spec-first AI guardrails and lightweight task workflow
body:
This PR addresses issue #269.

---

## Summary

This PR introduces a **spec-first documentation system** and a **lightweight, file-based task workflow** to make AI-assisted development in Zapstore safer, more predictable, and easier to review.

The focus is not on adding process, but on **making constraints explicit** and **reducing AI drift**, while keeping the system small and understandable.

---

## Motivation

As Zapstore increasingly uses AI for implementation, we observed recurring problems:

- AI drifting from original intent
- UX regressions caused by async or lifecycle mistakes
- “Helpful” refactors outside the intended scope
- Tests validating implementations instead of behavior
- Growing reliance on implicit rules embedded in prompts or `.cursorrules`

The core issue is the lack of a **clear, versioned contract between humans and AI**.

This PR establishes that contract.

---

## Guideline Specs (Source of Truth)

This PR introduces a small set of **human-owned guideline specs** under:

specs/guidelines/

These files change slowly and are the authoritative source of intent, boundaries, and constraints.

The following files are introduced or updated by this PR and serve as the authoritative guardrails:

- specs/guidelines/CONTEXT.md
- specs/guidelines/VISION.md
- specs/guidelines/ARCHITECTURE.md
- specs/guidelines/INVARIANTS.md
- specs/guidelines/QUALITY_BAR.md

### VISION.md

Defines what Zapstore is, who it is for, what success means, and explicit non-goals.

### ARCHITECTURE.md

Defines package responsibilities, ownership, and allowed / forbidden dependencies.
It intentionally avoids prescribing implementation or UI patterns.

### INVARIANTS.md

Defines **non-negotiable behavioral guarantees**, including:

- UI safety and non-blocking behavior
- lifecycle-safe async work
- local-first UX guarantees
- security and verification requirements

If an invariant is violated, the implementation is incorrect.

### QUALITY_BAR.md

Defines what “acceptable work” means:

- anti-patterns we explicitly reject
- behavior-focused testing expectations
- clear rules for human ↔ AI collaboration

---

## CONTEXT.md — Orientation Only

This PR also introduces CONTEXT.md.

Its role is **orientation only**, especially for AI agents:

- what this repository is
- high-level stack and structure
- where the authoritative rules live

It defines no behavior or constraints.
If it conflicts with any guideline spec, it is wrong.

---

## Task Workflow (Manus-inspired, intentionally adapted)

The execution workflow is inspired by Manus-style “planning with files”:

- https://github.com/OthmanAdi/planning-with-files

We adopt the core ideas:

- files as persistent working memory
- plan-first execution
- explicit progress tracking

And intentionally reject heavier mechanics:

- mandatory findings/progress logs
- mechanical rules such as the “2-action browser rule”

Zapstore is **code-centric and UX/safety-focused**, not research-centric.
The workflow is adapted accordingly to keep ceremony low.

---

## Feature Specs and Work Packets

### Feature Specs

Non-trivial features and behavior-affecting bugfixes use short **feature specs** under:

specs/features/

Feature specs are human-owned and define:

- the goal
- explicit non-goals
- user-visible behavior
- edge cases
- acceptance criteria

They define **what should happen**, not how.

A minimal template is provided to keep specs quick to write and easy to review.

---

### Work Packets

For non-trivial work, a temporary **work packet** is used. It consists of:

- a feature spec
- a task plan (task_plan.md)
- a test matrix
- optional decision notes

Work packets may be archived or deleted after merge.

---

## Task Plan Ownership

task_plan.md acts as the AI’s working memory.

- Humans seed it with a rough checklist.
- AI refines the plan, executes tasks, and marks progress.
- **Every code change must map to a task_plan item.**

If a spec is unclear or incorrect, the AI must stop and report a Spec Issue instead of guessing.

---

## Templates

Minimal templates are provided under:

work/\_template/

Templates are intentionally lightweight and non-authoritative.
They exist to reduce friction, not to define rules.
All authority remains in the guideline specs.

---

## Specs Directory Overview

For clarity, below is the expected high-level structure of the specs directory.

This is not a rigid schema, but a reference layout to make navigation and ownership obvious.

    specs/
      guidelines/
        CONTEXT.md
        VISION.md
        ARCHITECTURE.md
        INVARIANTS.md
        QUALITY_BAR.md
      features/
        _template.md
        FEAT-003-download-install-verify.md
        FEAT-004-zaps-nwc.md

    work/
      _template/
        task_plan.md
        test_matrix.md
        decisions.md
      FEAT-003-download-install-verify/
        task_plan.md
        test_matrix.md
        decisions.md

## Cursor Rules Simplification

This PR significantly simplifies .cursorrules.

Instead of embedding architectural or behavioral authority in a hidden prompt:

- durable rules live in versioned markdown
- .cursorrules becomes minimal and operational
- AI behavior becomes explicit and reviewable

---

## References and Inspiration

This work was informed by:

- https://github.com/OthmanAdi/planning-with-files
- https://github.com/damus-io/notedeck/blob/master/AGENTS.md
- https://github.com/alltheseas/damus/blob/patch-1/AGENTS.md

Rather than copying these approaches wholesale, we distilled the ideas most relevant to Zapstore:
UI safety, non-blocking guarantees, lifecycle correctness, local-first behavior, and reviewability.

---

## What This PR Does Not Do

- It does not redesign the architecture
- It does not freeze implementation or UI patterns
- It does not introduce heavy process or ceremony

The goal is **clarity, safety, and simplicity**.

---

## Expected Impact

- Clear, shared contract between humans and AI
- Less AI drift and fewer UX regressions
- Easier and more objective reviews
- A simpler, safer `.cursorrules`

---

## Suggested Validation (Pilot Workflow)

Since this PR introduces process and guardrails (not product features), a lightweight pilot is recommended before relying on it broadly.

Suggested pilot:
- Pick one non-trivial UX-sensitive change (async/lifecycle/security adjacent).
- Write a short feature spec under specs/features/ using the template.
- Create a work packet under work/FEAT-PILOT-*/ with task_plan.md + test_matrix.md (and optional decisions.md).
- Run one AI-assisted implementation strictly following the workflow (no spec edits during implementation).
- Review as if it were a real PR:
  - Every code change maps to task_plan.md
  - test_matrix.md covers failure modes and edge cases
  - no drift or unrelated refactors
- Capture any workflow friction and adjust templates or cursorrules minimally.

title: Fix NWC button crash and improve zap flow UX
body:
## Summary

This PR fixes a silent crash when tapping the "Setup NWC" button in the Lightning invoice toast, and improves the overall zap flow UX.

Resolves #275

## Changes

### 1. Fix BuildContext crash on "Setup NWC" button
The button was using a `BuildContext` from the `ZapAmountDialog` that had already been disposed after `Navigator.pop()`. This caused a `FlutterError: This BuildContext is no longer valid` crash when trying to open the NWC dialog.

**Solution:** Capture `rootNavigator` before closing the dialog and use `rootNavigator.context` for subsequent dialogs.

### 2. Rename and enhance NWC flow
- Renamed button from **"Setup NWC"** to **"Zap with NWC"**
- New `NWCZapDialog` now accepts the zap request and executes the payment inline after the user enters their NWC string
- Dialog buttons: **Cancel** and **"Zap X sats"**

### 3. Toast dismisses on action button tap
Toast now dismisses immediately when any action button is tapped, before executing the action.

### 4. Block dialog dismissal during zap execution
Added `PopScope` and `barrierDismissible: false` to prevent closing dialogs (via back button or tap outside) while a zap payment is in progress. This avoids crashes by ensuring the `BuildContext` remains valid for showing success/error toasts.

## Trade-off / Question

The current solution blocks user interaction during zap submission to preserve the `BuildContext`. 

An alternative approach would be to implement a `GlobalKey<NavigatorState>` at the app level, which would allow showing dialogs/toasts from anywhere without depending on widget context. However, this would require changes to:
- `main.dart` - create the global key
- `router.dart` - pass the key to MaterialApp/Navigator
- All dialog/toast call sites

**Should we consider migrating to the GlobalKey approach for a cleaner long-term solution?**

title: Allow managing App Catalog relays (kind 10067) — closes #205
body:
This PR implements **App Catalog relay management** so signed-in users can view and maintain their relay list (Nostr kind **10067**) used for app discovery.

Fixes **#205**.

---

## Summary
- Adds a **Profile → App Catalog Relays** UI for managing the user’s app discovery relays.
- Persists relay changes **locally** and publishes them to **bootstrap** relays.
- Ensures **Latest Releases**, **Updates**, and **Debug Info** react immediately to relay changes by using refresh tokens and subscription cancellation.

---

## What changed
### App Catalog Relay Management (Profile)
- New section in `ProfileScreen` to:
  - List current relays (shows full `ws://` / `wss://` scheme).
  - Add a relay with a **protocol dropdown** and improved input UX (disabled during operations, “+” button enabled only with text).
  - Remove a relay with proper UI feedback (skeleton state during add/remove).
- Relay input validation + normalization:
  - Rejects invalid hosts (e.g., `192.168.8/200`).
  - Normalizes host casing and strips trailing slashes.
  - Prevents duplicates by comparing **scheme + host + port (+ path)**, treating default ports consistently (e.g., `wss://relay.com` == `wss://relay.com:443`).

---

## Refresh + subscription behavior (to keep UI/Debug Info correct)
### Refresh tokens / providers
To force re-fetching and re-subscribing after relay changes, we introduced:
- `_appCatalogRelaysRefreshProvider` + `_appCatalogRelayListProvider` (Profile)
  - Uses a tokenized `subscriptionPrefix` so the relay list query can be invalidated and re-fetched after save/publish.
- `latestReleasesRefreshProvider` (Latest Releases)
  - Tokenized `subscriptionPrefix` (`latest-$token`) so a new streaming subscription is created when relays change.
- `updatesRefreshProvider` (Updates)
  - Tokenized `subscriptionPrefix` (`updates-$token` and `updates-profiles-$token`) so updates + author profile queries resubscribe on relay change.

### Cancelling stale subscriptions
When **removing** a relay, we explicitly cancel active subscriptions tied to the removed relay (via `models`/Purplebase APIs) so the **Debug Info** reflects the new state immediately and avoids keeping stale relay subscriptions alive.

---

## Known limitation (Purplebase local cache)
Purplebase uses a **local-first SQLite cache** for app data. Because of that:
- Relay override vs local cache: App Catalog relays do override/replace the default relay set for discovery going forward, but previously fetched apps can still remain visible because we don’t purge the local Purplebase cache when relays change.
- If this is bothersome, users can go to **Profile → Clear local storage** to fully reset cached content.

---

## Test plan
- Sign in.
- Go to **Profile → App Catalog Relays**.
- Add a relay (try both `ws://` and `wss://`); confirm it persists and publishes.
- Remove a relay; confirm:
  - UI updates immediately,
  - Debug Info no longer shows subscriptions involving the removed relay,
  - Latest Releases / Updates re-subscribe (new subscription prefixes).
- Verify duplicate prevention:
  - Try adding the same relay twice (including `wss://host` vs `wss://host:443`) → should be rejected.

title: Fix saved apps section stuck in loading or disappearing - #283
body:
## Fix saved apps section stuck in loading or disappearing

Fixes #283

### Problem

When the user had no saved apps, the "Saved Apps" section would either:
1. Get stuck in an infinite loading state
2. Briefly show content then disappear completely

### Root Cause

The issue had two parts:

1. **`_SavedAppsSection`** was using `.when()` on the `bookmarksProvider`, which would re-enter loading state during provider refresh, causing UI flicker.

2. **`_SavedAppsList`** was returning `SizedBox.shrink()` when the local query returned empty results. This happened because it shared a `hasLoadedOnce` flag with `_SavedAppsSection`, and when apps existed in bookmarks but weren't cached locally, the section would disappear entirely.

### Solution

- **Simplified `_SavedAppsHeading`**: Now always shows the heading when the user is signed in, regardless of bookmark state.

- **Refactored `_SavedAppsSection`**: Uses `valueOrNull` to preserve data during provider refresh instead of `.when()`, preventing the loading flicker.

- **Centralized empty state in `_SavedAppsList`**: All empty state logic now lives in one place. When there are no bookmarks or apps aren't found locally, it shows "No saved apps yet" instead of disappearing.

### Note on Empty State

Previously, when the user had no saved apps, the section would simply not render (no heading, no content). **We decided to add an explicit empty state** ("No saved apps yet") to provide better UX feedback.

If this behavior is not desired, we can revert to hiding the section entirely when empty by:
1. Removing the heading when there are no bookmarks
2. Returning `SizedBox.shrink()` instead of the empty state text

### Test Plan

- [ ] User with no saved apps → should see "Saved Apps" heading + "No saved apps yet"
- [ ] User with saved apps (cached locally) → should see the list of apps
- [ ] User with saved apps (not cached locally) → should see "No saved apps yet"
- [ ] Clear cache and reload → should not get stuck in loading

title: Fix background update notifications (WorkManager isolate) + installed apps snapshot (Fixes #262)
body: ## Fix background update notifications (WorkManager) — #262 Fixes #262 ### Problem Background update checks were silently skipping, so users were never notified about available updates. Root causes: - The background worker relied on `android_package_manager/events` (EventChannel), which is not reliably available in WorkManager’s headless isolate. This left the installed apps list empty and caused an early exit. - The background path did not consistently load the release → metadata/asset relationships required for `app.hasUpdate`, leading to false negatives. - Foreground and background could initialize Purplebase using different storage locations. - Weekly cleanup used incorrect file deletion logic. ### Solution Make background checks deterministic and independent of EventChannel streams: - Persist a small **installed apps snapshot** during foreground sync. - Load installed apps from this snapshot in background via a **BackgroundPackageManager** (no EventChannel usage). - Explicitly load `Release` + `FileMetadata` + `SoftwareAsset` before computing `hasUpdate`. - Use a **single DB location** (`ApplicationSupportDirectory`) in foreground and background. - Fix cleanup logic to safely delete files. ### Verification Background WorkManager task successfully delivers update notifications. ### Key changes - Background update logic no longer depends on EventChannel. - Correct `hasUpdate` computation in background. - Unified storage paths and safer cleanup. --- Fixes #262

title: Reproducible Android builds for F-Droid (config + CI proof)
body:
This PR introduces **reproducible / deterministic** Android APK builds and adds tooling to **verify reproducibility** on Linux amd64 (CI/Docker), with a local verification path (faster than Docker, still does two clean builds).

The motivation is F‑Droid compatibility and long‑term build verifiability.

Even if not merged immediately, this PR is intended to:
- document the reproducible‑build approach
- centralize technical discussion
- serve as a reference for future CI / F‑Droid integration

Related: [#69](https://github.com/zapstore/zapstore/issues/69)

## What changed (important)

This PR **does modify build‑related configuration**, specifically to:
- pin toolchain inputs
- avoid non‑deterministic build inputs
- produce **unsigned**, reproducible release APKs

**No application logic or runtime behavior is changed.**

## What’s included

- Dockerized build environment with pinned:
  - Flutter SDK
  - Android SDK / build‑tools
  - NDK
- Deterministic build setup (`SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH`, unsigned release)
-  GitHub Actions workflow integrated for reproducibility proof (**manual trigger only**; no automatic runs on push).
- **Host proof script** for local verification (`repro/prove_repro_host.sh`)
- **Arm64‑only fast path enabled by default**
  (`--target-platform android-arm64 --split-per-abi`)
- **Documentation** [`REPRODUCIBLE_BUILD.md`](https://github.com/zapstore/zapstore/blob/reproducible-build/REPRODUCIBLE_BUILD.md) (how to run the proofs and interpret results)


## Current status

- **Docker proof is reproducible** (two Linux amd64 builds produce identical APKs)
- **Host proof is reproducible** on the same machine (two local builds produce identical APKs)

## Scope & safety

- No changes to app code
- No signing or release logic touched
- All changes are limited to build / infra configuration

## Discussion

Feedback is welcome on:
- the chosen build flags
- toolchain pinning strategy
- whether this approach fits the project’s release and F‑Droid goals
